requirements.evidence: Contract fully present: queues/tickets migrations with cascades, unique (entity_id,slug)/(queue_id,code) and the (queue_id,status,priority,issued_at) index (database/migrations/2026_10_29_035657_create_queues_table.php:11-22, 2026_10_29_035658_create_tickets_table.php:14-27); IssueTicket locks and re-reads the queue state inside the transaction, rejects inactive/negative priority and retries collisions (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:32-58); Ticket::nextCode implements last-valid-by-insertion-order including A999->A1000 and malformed-code skipping (app/Models/Ticket.php:88-106); Ticket::call locks the row, enforces single call and records status/called_at/called_by (app/Models/Ticket.php:114-136); models, enums, exception, factories and the Entity::queues() relation match the contract (app/Models/Queue.php:11-38, app/Models/Entity.php:47-50, database/factories/TicketFactory.php:21-49). Docs/business-rules.md:70-105 and docs/database-schema.md:151-163 were updated as required.

security.evidence: Ticket::call authorizes the caller through Gate::forUser(...)->authorize('call', $ticket) before any write (app/Models/Ticket.php:122), and TicketPolicy restricts to entity members (app/Policies/TicketPolicy.php:15); the test 'a user outside the ticket entity cannot call' asserts the ticket is unchanged (tests/Feature/Ticket/TicketCallTest.php:70-82); mass assignment is bounded by the fillable attributes (app/Models/Ticket.php:16-25, app/Models/Queue.php:11); negative priority is rejected server-side (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:28-30); the queue state is read from the locked database row, not the passed model (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:35-41). No UI/escaping or secret-handling concerns apply.

A999->A1000, malformed A-X, deletion (tests/Feature/Ticket/TicketModelTest.php:39-131), immutability (TicketModelTest.php:145-162), issuance incl. stale queue and negative priority (tests/Feature/Ticket/IssueTicketTest.php:32-82), call happy path, unauthorized stranger/other entity and double-call (tests/Feature/Ticket/TicketCallTest.php:32-91). simplicity.evidence: Minimal implementation: nextCode is one query plus a scan (app/Models/Ticket.php:88-106), the immutability rule is a single updating hook with a const allow-list (Ticket.php:35-70), call() reuses a transaction + forceFill (Ticket.php:114-136) and the action is a short closure with one retry loop (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:32-58). No service/repository layer or speculative abstraction; factories are tiny (database/factories/QueueFactory.php:20-29, TicketFactory.php:21-49). Only nit: nextCode plucks every code of the queue into memory (Ticket.php:90-93).

readability.evidence: Clear names, small focused methods and useful docblocks throughout (app/Models/Ticket.php:82-114, app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:17-27, both factories); style matches the generated Laravel/entity pattern. Nits only: IssueTicket's docblock omits the RuntimeException it throws (app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:17-22 vs :58) and the caller-instance sync via setRawAttributes(...) is unexplained (app/Models/Ticket.php:134).

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: domain models/enums/exception/policy/action, two migrations, two factories, four feature tests and the required docs. The additional docs/README.md:12, docs/architecture.md:130 and CHANGELOG.md edits are small, convention-mandated doc sync tied to this feature; no unrelated refactors or features.

issues.explanation: The retry-on-unique-collision branch (including the final RuntimeException at line 58) has no test, so a required failure path ships untested despite the project's 'everything implemented ships with a test' rule.

Because the next code is derived from the newest still-present valid code, deleting the most recently issued ticket makes its number reusable (A001..A003, delete A003 -> next A003), which conflicts with the business rule 'deleting a ticket does not reuse its number'; the documented example only covers deleting a middle ticket, so the ambiguity should be confirmed (the docs hedge it at docs/business-rules.md:96-99).

Both models rely on the #[Fillable] attribute; composer.json is not in the diff, so confirm the project's Laravel version actually provides Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes\Fillable (conventions require matching the pinned version) — otherwise the models are effectively unguarded/unfillable.
The __invoke docblock lists InactiveQueueException and InvalidArgumentException but not the RuntimeException thrown after five failed allocation attempts, so the public contract is incomplete.

Synchronising the caller's model with $this->setRawAttributes($ticket->getAttributes(), true) is an obscure one-liner; assigning the three call fields or calling refresh() would be easier for the next maintainer to follow.
nextCode() plucks every code for the queue into memory to find the newest valid one; a paginated/lazy scan or a max-with-fallback query would avoid memory growth on queues with a long history.

review.summary: The change implements the queue/ticket domain core end to end: migrations with the required keys and cascade/index rules, Queue/Ticket models with relations, casts and a write-once guard, per-queue A001-style code allocation with malformed-code skipping, a policy-guarded single call, the IssueTicket action with a locked inactive-queue re-check and collision retry, factories, tests, and the required documentation updates. It is well scoped, readable and secure, and virtually every contract item is covered; the main gap is the untested unique-collision retry path, plus a few nits (documented throws, delete-newest code reuse ambiguity, version-sensitive #[Fillable]).
